title: Linking through unique identifier in location history
description: Location history data stored in DS2 likely contains unique identifiers (user IDs, device IDs, session IDs) that can be used to link data records to specific individuals across different sessions.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in location data
description: Location history data contains combinations of attributes (timestamps, locations, movement patterns) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to individuals when combined with other information.

title: Profiling an individual through pattern analysis
description: The analytics service explicitly derives 'daily routine and movement patterns' from location history, which constitutes profiling an individual through analysis of their data for behavioral patterns.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The data store contains and provides identified location history data that is processed by the analytics service to derive patterns about individuals.

title: Identifier in location history data
description: Location history data contains unique references to the identity of data subjects through user identifiers, device identifiers, or session identifiers embedded in the data.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location data reveals sensitive attributes about individuals including their whereabouts, movement patterns, and daily routines, which supports identification of data subjects.

title: Sensitive location data type collected
description: Location history is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required for the stated functionality.

title: Fine-grained location data granularity
description: Location history data is processed at a fine-grained level (individual session locations) that may be more detailed than functionally needed for deriving daily routine patterns.

title: Excessive volume of location data processed
description: Location history is queried 'across sessions' suggesting an excessive amount of personal data is processed beyond what is functionally needed for pattern derivation.

title: Unnecessary pattern analysis and enrichment
description: Deriving daily routine and movement patterns constitutes additional treatment, analysis, and enrichment of personal data that may not be necessary for the core functionality.

title: Data propagation to analytics service
description: Location history data is propagated from the data store to the analytics service where it may be accessible by parties beyond the original collection purpose.

title: Unawareness of location data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location history is being queried across sessions and analyzed to derive daily routine and movement patterns.

title: Lack of control over location data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location history is processed, analyzed, and what patterns are derived from it.

title: Lack of control over rectification and erasure of location data
description: Data subjects may lack control to rectify incorrect location data or remove location history that is no longer relevant for pattern analysis.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing location history across multiple sessions to derive detailed movement patterns may process more personal data than actually needed for the stated functionality.

title: Lawfulness problems with automated decision making
description: Automated derivation of daily routine and movement patterns from location data may constitute automated decision-making that requires specific lawful grounds and may involve sensitive personal data.

title: Profiling of individual through health condition inference
description: The app analyzes user data to infer eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals, creating a profile that links data to the individual user.
assumptions: The app has access to sufficient health-related data to make these inferences.

title: Linking through unique user identifier
description: The app uses unique identifiers to link health data to specific users, enabling data association across the system.
assumptions: User identifiers are maintained and used for data linkage.

title: Revealing health attributes disclosed to user
description: The dashboard displays health condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk) which are revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject's health status.
assumptions: Health indicators are displayed to the user and may be visible to others.

title: Processing of identified health data
description: The system processes identified user data to generate and display health trend indicators and risk signals.
assumptions: User data is identified and processed for health analytics.

title: System response reveals health condition information
description: The existence and nature of health conditions (eating-disorder or diabetes risk) is revealed through the system's display response to the user.
assumptions: The dashboard display inherently reveals the user's health status.

title: Sensitive health data types collected and displayed
description: Health data (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) is highly sensitive and may be collected and displayed beyond what is strictly required for basic app functionality.
assumptions: Health data is more sensitive than typical app data and requires careful handling.

title: Data analysis and enrichment for health inference
description: Personal data is analyzed and enriched to infer health conditions, which may be beyond what is functionally necessary for basic app operation.
assumptions: The inference process adds complexity beyond basic data display.

title: User unawareness of health data processing
description: Users may not be fully aware of how their health data is being collected, processed, and used to generate risk indicators.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities.

title: Lack of user control over health data preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their health data is processed and displayed.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not adequately cover health data processing.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal health data may be processed than is actually needed to display basic health trends and risk indicators.
assumptions: Health data collection may exceed functional requirements.

title: Automated decision making on sensitive health data
description: Automated inference of eating-disorder or diabetes risk may constitute automated decision-making on sensitive personal data, raising GDPR lawfulness concerns.
assumptions: Health risk signals are generated through automated processing without adequate safeguards.
uncertainty_note: Assumes automated decision-making applies to health risk inference.
